clue.text: Leading one of each clue is to be taken

definitions.text: Leading one of each clue is to be taken

parts.words: Leading one of each clue is to be taken
parts.note: an instruction to the solver: the opening character of every across clue should be read off, and the thing so read is the answer

explanation.surface: A puzzle rule telling the solver to pick something from the start of every clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the across clues in order spell LOOK AT THE LETTERS, so this entry is both a definition and the key to a hidden message.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading character of a written clue is one symbol of the alphabet, which is what the solver is told to take.

clue.text: In French little Susan has to follow

parts.note: the French word for in is en
Sue is the short form of the name Susan

explanation.surface: In France, young Susan is obliged to tag along behind someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a consequence is to follow on, a synonym.

clue.text: Nurse could give this surprise to people given time

parts.note: a treat is an unexpected pleasure, a surprise
men means people in the general old sense

explanation.surface: A nurse hands out an unexpected gift to patients when they have been given some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Care or medical attention is what a nurse provides to a patient.

clue.text: They're up for propositions to be deduced

definitions.meaning: people mounted on horses are said to be up, as jockeys are
in geometry a rider is a subsidiary problem worked out from a theorem already proved

explanation.surface: Some people are keen to see arguments worked out to a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeys on horseback are up in the saddle, and a geometry exercise appended to a theorem is called a rider.

clue.text: Old manuscripts they explain, and they put a shine on things

definitions.meaning: scholars who write marginal notes on old texts are glossators or commentators

definitions.text: they put a shine on things
definitions.meaning: polishers give things a lustre or gloss

explanation.surface: A team who both annotate ancient texts and polish objects.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloss is both a marginal commentary and a sheen, so one who supplies either is a commentator or a polisher.

clue.text: Here novel abdominal pain is?

parts.note: the title of a famous novel read literally answers where stomach discomfort from trapped gas has vanished to

explanation.surface: Asking where some unusual stomach ache has got to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is a British word for trapped gas causing stomach pain; Margaret Mitchell's novel title, read literally, says that pain has departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's Civil War novel bears this title, and read literally it means the stomach complaint has vanished.

clue.text: Endless pomp daily around in celebration of games

indicators.note: around here means mixed about, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the word pomp is cut off, leaving it without its end

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ceremonial display every day surrounds a sporting festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims pomp to POM; 'around' then rearranges POM with DAILY to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern Olympic Games, or a celebration of them, is called by this name.

clue.text: Deadly sin makes one quiet about much

indicators.note: about means going round, so the call for quiet is placed outside the next word

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a lot means much

explanation.surface: A wicked vice is to silence someone over a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness is one of the seven deadly sins of Christian tradition.

clue.text: It falls in rugged terrain around West Africa

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go outside the next piece
rugged suggests something roughened and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
WA is a short form of West Africa

explanation.surface: Something comes down across rough land in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It falls' looks like the start of a sentence about the land, but it is the whole definition; 'rugged' and 'around' do the work in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation that drops from clouds is water in liquid form coming down from the sky.

clue.text: On the rise in this new case and arresting 100 in New York

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so New York takes in the Roman number

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A fresh legal case in New York involves an arrest, and its prospects are improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal and 'arresting' means holding. The definition rests on the idiom 'in the ascendancy', meaning on the rise, with 'this' standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gaining power or dominance is to be in the ascendancy, so the definition names the state the idiom describes.

clue.text: K's alternative in old Information Technology is to drop

indicators.note: in places the thousand symbol inside the following letters

parts.note: K and M both stand for a thousand, so one can replace the other

explanation.surface: In dated computing, one letter stands in for another, so something gets left out.
explanation.walkthrough: K (kilo) and M (Roman mille) both mean a thousand, so M is K's alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out or skip it is a synonym of dropping it.

clue.text: two vitamins in a group of cells

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'two vitamins in a group of cells' (5,3): the opening word is missing (the first letters of the across clues spell LOOK AT THE LETTERS, so the clue began with an A word), and nothing supplies THROW after D + E + A.
annotationWithheld.clue: two vitamins in a group of cells

clue.text: They show contempt, as an afterthought, about playwright

indicators.note: about means the postscript letters go round the playwright

parts.note: PS, the postscript, is something added as an afterthought
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Late remarks about a dramatist express scorn for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a plural noun: exclamations of disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamations of disdain or impatience are things that express scorn.

clue.text: This child has to live without salt

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the verb goes round the sailor

parts.note: to be means to exist or live
a salt is an old sailor, AB being an able seaman

explanation.surface: A youngster must get by with no salt in the diet.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant or very young child is a synonym.

clue.text: Wooden statues featured in this carol, maybe

indicators.note: maybe says these letters are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Statues carved from wood appear in a Christmas song.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient statues with a wooden trunk and stone head and limbs are given this name.

clue.text: Hideous misrepresentation of attempt to hide an undergarment?

indicators.note: to hide means to cover up, so the attempt goes round the garment

parts.note: try means an attempt
a vest is a British undershirt

explanation.surface: Trying to conceal one's underwear is a ghastly distortion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt worn next to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque parody or distortion of something is a synonym.

clue.text: Good at spotting European with a leg broken, I'd reported

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reported signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: the contraction I'd is said like the word meaning looked at

explanation.surface: A European with a broken leg tells everyone he was vigilant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns A LEG into AGLE; 'reported' turns I'D into its sound-alike, EYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Having very sharp vision, like the bird of prey, makes someone good at noticing things.

clue.text: Outer edges of roads, say, badly affected — extra snow initially about

indicators.note: about means the outer pieces go round the anagram

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of reach, counted as an extra run

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of snow
badly affected signals the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Verges, for instance, suffer badly as more snow arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly affected' signals the anagram and 'about' the container. In cricket a wide is a delivery out of the batter's reach, which counts as an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: Verges or roadsides are the strips at the margins of a road.

clue.text: Extend pamphlet written by expert

indicators.note: written by puts the writer first, so the expert comes before the pamphlet

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: A specialist writes a booklet to lengthen something.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong or draw out in time is a synonym.

clue.text: Life-blood about after function

indicators.note: after places the word for about behind the function word

parts.note: to go is to function or work
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The essence of something comes after its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt blood, especially clotted, is a synonym for blood.

clue.text: Nerves aplenty here? It's a lot of money!

definitions.meaning: a nervous person is called a ... of nerves, a cluster of nerve fibres
slang for a large sum of cash

explanation.surface: Someone anxious discovers it is a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight cluster of fibres is so named, as is a large amount of cash in slang.

clue.text: Embraces 150 snakes

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: One hundred and fifty serpents wrap themselves round something.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug is to hold closely, a synonym for embraces.

clue.text: A bout of drinking upset peers

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobles are put out by a heavy session in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge or session of heavy drinking is a synonym.

clue.text: The European Union hosts Conservative workers in charge of get-together

indicators.note: hosts means holding within, so the union contains the party letter

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation
men are workers

explanation.surface: The EU invites Tory labourers to take charge of a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: relating to a coming together of churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting unity or a meeting of different churches is the sense of the word, an adjective of universal assembly.

clue.text: Landlord's place on English river, private

parts.note: a landlord runs a pub or inn

explanation.surface: A pub owner's house beside an English river is secluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden or personal, as in inner thoughts, is a synonym for private.

clue.text: Traitors brought back by Polaris?.

indicators.note: brought back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rats are traitors or deserters

explanation.surface: Deserters return guided by the North Star.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole star is an example of a bright celestial body.

clue.text: Eliminating moisture, wimp, right-winger, set gin

parts.note: a drip is a feeble person
a dry is a hardline Conservative in British politics

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of a weakling, a rightist and a drink being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: In Thatcher-era British politics a 'dry' was a hardline right-wing Tory. 'set' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging up clothes to lose water without wringing is a way of getting them dry.

clue.text: Ran down essentially in potentially sad surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the anagram goes round the Latin phrase
potentially means the letters could become something else, an anagram

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, essentially

explanation.surface: He fled downhill, at heart in a mournful setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' turns SAD into ASD, which surrounds PER SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or disparage someone is to run them down.

clue.text: Some sudden duress to bear

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of unexpected pressure is something to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or put up with is a synonym for bearing hardship.
